deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the second page of Riemann's letter to Weierstrass (autumn 1859), which accompanied the submission of 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse' to the Berlin Academy. The previous page gives the explicit formula
 f(x) = Li(x) - Σ_α [Li(x^{1/2+αi}) + Li(x^{1/2-αi})] + ∫_x^∞ dt/((t^2-1) t log t) + log ξ(0),
with f(x) = Σ_{n≥1} (1/n) F(x^{1/n}). In modern notation f = Π(x) = J(x), Riemann's prime-power counting function.

This page contains no new derivation. It completes the statement and then lists what still needs proof.

(1) Inversion. The page completes the formula F(x) = Σ_m (-1)^μ (1/m) f(x^{1/m}). Here m runs over the squarefree integers and μ is the number of prime factors of m. In modern terms this is Möbius inversion of f(x) = Σ_n F(x^{1/n})/n, namely π(x) = Σ_m μ(m)/m · J(x^{1/m}).

(2) Admitted gap. Riemann writes that the proof is not completely carried out. Two statements that the paper only asserts are said to follow from an expansion of ξ that he had not yet simplified enough to communicate.

(a) Zero count. Between 0 and T there are 'about' (T/2π) log(T/2π) - T/2π real roots of ξ(α)=0. Riemann's ξ(t) is ξ(1/2+it) in modern notation, so a real α corresponds to a zero on the critical line. Two points stand out:
- The modern Riemann–von Mangoldt formula counts all zeros with 0 < Im ρ < T. Riemann's wording here, as in the paper, says real roots, i.e. zeros on the critical line.
- This is the much-discussed claim from the paper that 'about this many real roots' exist.

(b) Convergence of the sum over zeros. Order the terms of Σ_α [Li(x^{1/2+αi}) + Li(x^{1/2-αi})] by increasing α. The series then converges to the same limit as
 (1/(2πi log x)) ∫_{a-bi}^{a+bi} d/ds[(1/s) log(ξ((s-1/2)i)/ξ(0))] x^s ds as b → ∞.

Sign check (my derivation). In the paper,
 f(x) = -(1/(2πi log x)) ∫ d/ds[(log ζ(s))/s] x^s ds.
The completed ξ enters log ζ(s) with a + sign, through ζ(s) = ξ / (Π(s/2) (s-1) π^{-s/2}). Hence the contribution of log(ξ/ξ(0)) to f is minus this integral. Since that contribution equals -Σ_α(...), the series equals plus the integral, exactly as written in the letter. Also ξ is even, so ξ((s-1/2)i) = ξ(-i(s-1/2)), which is Riemann's ξ evaluated at t with s = 1/2+ti.

(3) Remainder of the page. The rest is administrative:
- The paper is too long for the Monatsberichte; he hopes the result and some remarks will be printed there.
- He asks that, if the proof is criticised, it be noted that he himself pointed out the needed supplements.
- He asks to be told what will be printed.
- Alternatives: Borchardt's Journal, or a memoir in the Göttingen Societät proceedings (Weber's offer), which he would undertake only reluctantly.

The 'expansion of ξ' mentioned here is plausibly connected to the asymptotic material later found in the Nachlass by Siegel (the Riemann–Siegel formula, 1932).
errors: No mathematical errors. The integral's sign and normalization agree with the 1859 paper.

The phrase 'etwa ... reelle Wurzeln' (about so many real roots) in the zero-count claim remains unproved even today. Von Mangoldt proved the count for all zeros in the strip, not for zeros on the critical line. Riemann's assertion that it follows from an expansion of ξ is unverified.
Conditional convergence of the sum over zeros, when ordered by |α|, was proved only by von Mangoldt (1895). Riemann acknowledges the gap here.

deep.surprise_reason: This is Riemann's known letter to Weierstrass (1859); it is published and discussed in the literature. The mathematical content restates the 1859 paper. The admission that the zero count and the convergence follow from a not-yet-simplified expansion of ξ is historically interesting, but it is already known to historians.

checkable.asserts: Gives ≈29.0, matching the 29 nontrivial zeros with 0<Im<100. This checks the main term of Riemann's zero count; the +7/8 term is von Mangoldt's refinement.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import primepi, mobius, integer_nthroot; J=lambda x: sum(Rational(1,n)*primepi(integer_nthroot(x,n)[0]) for n in range(1,int(log(x,2))+2)); x=1000; sum(mobius(m)*Rational(1,m)*J(integer_nthroot(x,m)[0]) for m in range(1,11)) == primepi(x)
checkable.asserts: Möbius inversion π(x)=Σ μ(m)/m J(x^{1/m}) at a non-prime x. Floor-integer roots suffice for counting. The value (-1)^μ on squarefree m equals mobius(m).
d/ds li(x^s) = x^s/s. This underlies the relation between the Li terms and the contour integral with the 1/log x prefactor. It holds for real x>1 and real s on the principal branch.

transcription_corrections: 'Sollte man meinen Beweis eher ihn mitzutheilen' probably reads 'ehe ihn mitzutheilen' (i.e. before communicating it).
In the integral's upper limit the manuscript shows a struck-through character before 'a+bi'; the limits a-bi to a+bi are correct.
'ein [-Pl-]Plätzchen' – the struck letters are a false start of 'Plätzchen'; the reading is plausible.
'[-folgen-] aus einer Entwicklung': the struck word at the start of the line confirms that 'folgen' was moved to after 'ξ'.
